/-!
# Conjecture 9.1

by R. B. J. T. Allenby

A group $G$ is said to be *potent* if, to each $x \in G$ and each positive integer $n$
dividing the order of $x$ (we suppose $\infty$ is divisible by every positive integer),
there exists a finite homomorphic image of $G$ in which the image of $x$ has order
precisely $n$. Is the free product of two potent groups again potent?

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

blocks.code:
def IsPotent (G : Type u) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ (x : G) (n : ℕ), 0 < n → n ∣ orderOf x →
    ∃ (H : Type u) (_ : Group H) (_ : Finite H) (f : G →* H),
      Function.Surjective f ∧ orderOf (f x) = n
blocks.docstring:
A group $G$ is *potent* if, to each $x \in G$ and each positive integer $n$ dividing the
order of $x$, there exists a finite homomorphic image of $G$ in which the image of $x$ has
order precisely $n$.

An element of infinite order has `orderOf x = 0`, and every `n` divides `0`, so this matches
the convention that $\infty$ is divisible by every positive integer.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Mathlib has no residual-finiteness/finite-quotient predicate of this shape; `Subgroup.FiniteIndex` + `QuotientGroup` could express the same thing via finite-index normal subgroups, but the surjective-homomorphism-onto-a-finite-group form mirrors the source text ('finite homomorphic image') directly.
justification.name: Kourovka.«9.1».IsPotent
justification.why_needed: Neither Mathlib nor FormalConjecturesForMathlib has the notion of a potent group (rg for 'potent' only finds idempotent/nilpotent/unipotent). Defined as: for every x : G and every n : ℕ with 0 < n and n ∣ orderOf x, there exist a group H in the same universe as G with [Finite H] and a surjective f : G →* H such that orderOf (f x) = n. Two proved `category test` lemmas (trivial group is potent; every finite abelian group is potent) check the definition.

@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isPotent_of_subsingleton (G : Type u) [Group G] [Subsingleton G] : IsPotent G := by
  intro x n hn hdvd
  rw [Subsingleton.elim x 1, orderOf_one, Nat.dvd_one] at hdvd
  exact ⟨G, inferInstance, inferInstance, MonoidHom.id G, Function.surjective_id, by
    simp [hdvd, Subsingleton.elim x 1]⟩

blocks.code:
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isPotent_of_finite_of_commGroup (G : Type u) [CommGroup G] [Finite G] : IsPotent G := by
  intro x n hn hdvd
  refine ⟨G ⧸ Subgroup.zpowers (x ^ n), inferInstance, inferInstance, QuotientGroup.mk' _,
    QuotientGroup.mk'_surjective _, ?_⟩
  rw [orderOf_eq_iff hn]
  refine ⟨?_, fun m hm hm0 h => ?_⟩
  · rw [← map_pow, QuotientGroup.mk'_apply, QuotientGroup.eq_one_iff]
    exact Subgroup.mem_zpowers _
  · rw [← map_pow, QuotientGroup.mk'_apply, QuotientGroup.eq_one_iff,
      Subgroup.mem_zpowers_iff] at h
    obtain ⟨k, hk⟩ := h
    rw [← zpow_natCast, ← zpow_mul, ← zpow_natCast x m, zpow_eq_zpow_iff_modEq] at hk
    have h2 : (n : ℤ) ∣ (m : ℤ) := by
      have h3 : (n : ℤ) ∣ (m : ℤ) - n * k :=
        dvd_trans (Int.natCast_dvd_natCast.mpr hdvd) hk.dvd
      simpa using dvd_add h3 (dvd_mul_right (n : ℤ) k)
    exact absurd (Nat.le_of_dvd hm0 (Int.natCast_dvd_natCast.mp h2)) (not_le.mpr hm)

blocks.text:
/--
Is the free product $G * H$ of two potent groups $G$ and $H$ again potent?

The free product of groups is Mathlib's coproduct `Monoid.Coprod G H`, written `G ∗ H`.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«9.1» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G H : Type) [Group G] [Group H], IsPotent G → IsPotent H → IsPotent (G ∗ H) := by
  sorry

claims.decomposer_note: Single yes/no question (∀ potent groups G, H, the free product G * H — Mathlib's `Monoid.Coprod`/free product of groups — is potent); the preceding sentence only defines 'potent': for every x ∈ G and every positive integer n dividing the order of x (with infinite order counted as divisible by every n, which matches Mathlib's convention `orderOf x = 0` and `n ∣ 0`), there is a surjective homomorphism from G onto a finite group sending x to an element of order exactly n; the quantifier is over all pairs of potent groups, and n must be restricted to positive integers (n ≠ 0).
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates state the same faithful content: bespoke `IsPotent G` := ∀ x, ∀ n > 0, n ∣ orderOf x → ∃ finite group Q and surjective hom f : G →* Q with orderOf (f x) = n (Mathlib's `orderOf x = 0` for infinite order makes `n ∣ 0` hold for every positive n, exactly the notebook's '∞ divisible by every positive integer' convention; the positivity hypothesis excludes the degenerate n = 0); the question is `answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (G H : Type) [Group G] [Group H], IsPotent G → IsPotent H → IsPotent (G ∗ H)` with `Monoid.Coprod` (which carries Mathlib's `Group` instance and is the free product of groups). `answer(True)` = yes, quantifiers all after `answer`. c03 was chosen because CONTRIBUTING.md asks for basic API tests of bespoke definitions and c03 has the best ones (trivial group, and every finite abelian group is potent — a genuine non-vacuity check), all proved and compiling. Only edit: added a sentence to the main theorem docstring naming `Monoid.Coprod G H` for `G ∗ H`.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 9.1

by R. B. J. T. Allenby

A group $G$ is said to be *potent* if, to each $x \in G$ and each positive integer $n$
dividing the order of $x$ (we suppose $\infty$ is divisible by every positive integer),
there exists a finite homomorphic image of $G$ in which the image of $x$ has order
precisely $n$. Is the free product of two potent groups again potent?

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

open scoped Monoid.Coprod

namespace Kourovka.«9.1»

universe u

/-- A group $G$ is *potent* if, to each $x \in G$ and each positive integer $n$ dividing the
order of $x$, there exists a finite homomorphic image of $G$ in which the image of $x$ has
order precisely $n$.

An element of infinite order has `orderOf x = 0`, and every `n` divides `0`, so this matches
the convention that $\infty$ is divisible by every positive integer. -/
def IsPotent (G : Type u) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ (x : G) (n : ℕ), 0 < n → n ∣ orderOf x →
    ∃ (H : Type u) (_ : Group H) (_ : Finite H) (f : G →* H),
      Function.Surjective f ∧ orderOf (f x) = n

/-- The trivial group is potent. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isPotent_of_subsingleton (G : Type u) [Group G] [Subsingleton G] : IsPotent G := by
  intro x n hn hdvd
  rw [Subsingleton.elim x 1, orderOf_one, Nat.dvd_one] at hdvd
  exact ⟨G, inferInstance, inferInstance, MonoidHom.id G, Function.surjective_id, by
    simp [hdvd, Subsingleton.elim x 1]⟩

/-- Every finite abelian group is potent. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isPotent_of_finite_of_commGroup (G : Type u) [CommGroup G] [Finite G] : IsPotent G := by
  intro x n hn hdvd
  refine ⟨G ⧸ Subgroup.zpowers (x ^ n), inferInstance, inferInstance, QuotientGroup.mk' _,
    QuotientGroup.mk'_surjective _, ?_⟩
  rw [orderOf_eq_iff hn]
  refine ⟨?_, fun m hm hm0 h => ?_⟩
  · rw [← map_pow, QuotientGroup.mk'_apply, QuotientGroup.eq_one_iff]
    exact Subgroup.mem_zpowers _
  · rw [← map_pow, QuotientGroup.mk'_apply, QuotientGroup.eq_one_iff,
      Subgroup.mem_zpowers_iff] at h
    obtain ⟨k, hk⟩ := h
    rw [← zpow_natCast, ← zpow_mul, ← zpow_natCast x m, zpow_eq_zpow_iff_modEq] at hk
    have h2 : (n : ℤ) ∣ (m : ℤ) := by
      have h3 : (n : ℤ) ∣ (m : ℤ) - n * k :=
        dvd_trans (Int.natCast_dvd_natCast.mpr hdvd) hk.dvd
      simpa using dvd_add h3 (dvd_mul_right (n : ℤ) k)
    exact absurd (Nat.le_of_dvd hm0 (Int.natCast_dvd_natCast.mp h2)) (not_le.mpr hm)

/--
Is the free product $G * H$ of two potent groups $G$ and $H$ again potent?

The free product of groups is Mathlib's coproduct `Monoid.Coprod G H`, written `G ∗ H`.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«9.1» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G H : Type) [Group G] [Group H], IsPotent G → IsPotent H → IsPotent (G ∗ H) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«9.1»

items: 'Finite homomorphic image of G' is formalized as a surjective monoid hom f : G →* H onto a group H with [Finite H]; H is taken in the same universe as G, which loses nothing since every homomorphic image G/N lives there and every finite group is isomorphic to one in any universe.

'Positive integer n dividing the order of x' is formalized as `0 < n → n ∣ orderOf x`; infinite order is `orderOf x = 0`, and `n ∣ 0` holds for all n, matching the notebook's convention that ∞ is divisible by every positive integer. The `0 < n` hypothesis is essential: without it n = 0 would divide orderOf x = 0 and demand an element of infinite order in a finite group.
The main theorem quantifies over groups in `Type` (universe 0), following the convention of the existing Kourovka files (1_40, 19_25, 20_76).

The free product is `Monoid.Coprod G H` (notation `G ∗ H`, opened via `open scoped Monoid.Coprod`), which carries Mathlib's `Group` instance when G and H are groups; this is the free product of two groups.
Category `research open` and `AMS 20` (group theory); the two auxiliary lemmas are tagged `category test` and are fully proved.

reviewer_notes: No omissions by any candidate; all compiled with no warnings other than the expected sorry. Differences among candidates were cosmetic only (n ≠ 0 vs 0 < n; codomain universe `Type` vs same universe as G — harmless since the codomain is finite; universe-polymorphic vs `Type` for G, H — `Type` follows the existing Kourovka files; `G ∗ H` notation vs `Monoid.Coprod G H` — the scoped notation compiles without clash). Modelling note: 'finite homomorphic image' is taken as a surjective homomorphism onto a finite group, equivalent to a quotient by a finite-index normal subgroup. Final file compiled via `lake env lean --json` with only the `declaration uses 'sorry'` warning on the research-open theorem.
